records.name: WhatsApp notification transport for the MYTHOS GitHub bridge (Evolution API / wa-evolution / WAHA; MultiWA / WaSphere identified, not shortlisted)
records.repository: evolution-foundation/evolution-api (EvolutionAPI/evolution-api redirects here) · jfelipesjc/wa-evolution (+ jfelipesjc/wa-go) · devlikeapro/waha · identified only: ribato22/MultiWA, wasphere/wasphere
records.license: Evolution API: Apache-2.0 + two additional conditions (frontend logo/copyright retention; a Usage Notification Requirement — a visible 'Evolution API is being utilized' notice for administrators in docs/settings, else a commercial licence may be required; GitHub classifies it NOASSERTION) · wa-evolution: MIT (wa-go: MIT) · WAHA: Apache-2.0, and since 2026.6.1 there is no Core/Plus split and no separate Plus image
records.purpose: Deliver one outbound plain-text message when a GitHub control task reaches COMPLETED, FAILED, BLOCKED or the bridge blocked-for-a-human condition.
records.integration_method: NOT vendored and NOT deployed. What was built is the adapter boundary: projects/mythos-ai-executor/bridge/notify/{whatsapp.js,http-json.js,providers/evolution.js,providers/generic.js}. Evolution API is implemented as the default adapter (POST /message/sendText/{instance}, apikey header) and is selected at runtime by MYTHOS_BRIDGE_WHATSAPP_PROVIDER; the layer is disabled unless explicitly configured and enabled. gh-issue-147 added providers/generic.js, a configuration-driven adapter (path / auth header / JSON body template / message-id path) so that pointing MYTHOS at ANY other HTTP WhatsApp gateway is an environment change, not a new file — its defaults reproduce the Evolution shape byte for byte and that equivalence is asserted by test. Node core only, no npm dependency, no database (the executor store convention is reused for the idempotency ledger).
dependencies: a self-hosted WhatsApp gateway reachable on a private network (not deployed)
records.maintenance: LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-09-04 (WA-PROVIDER-2) via api.github.com, raw repository files, hub.docker.com and ghcr.io: Evolution API 9,528 stars, pushed 2026-07-14, 208 open issues, no stable release for 9 months, image evoapicloud/evolution-api:latest 389 MB compressed (already pulled on this host: 1.83 GB on disk, no container), vendor minimum 'at least 2GB of available RAM' + PostgreSQL/MySQL + Redis (4-container compose). wa-evolution 0 stars / 0 forks / 1 contributor, created 2026-06-26, pushed 2026-08-01, 12 tags in 5 weeks, CI with go test -race; single static Go binary + embedded SQLite, no services; ghcr image 9.6 MB (linux/amd64 compressed); built on the same author's from-scratch WhatsApp Web protocol stack wa-go (1 star). WAHA 7,334 stars, pushed 2026-09-01, monthly releases, 2 core maintainers, 2.48 M pulls; image 1,156 MB compressed (Chromium included; NOWEB/GOWS engines need no browser); vendor docs publish no RAM figure. Footprints are image sizes and vendor statements, NOT measurements on this host (gate step 3 still owed).
records.security: credential read at send time from a 0600 file, never stored/logged/echoed; gateway host must be loopback/RFC1918/single-label unless MYTHOS_BRIDGE_WHATSAPP_ALLOW_PUBLIC=1; every message passes the shared redaction; recipients and instance names validated against injection. The generic adapter's body template is JSON-parsed BEFORE substitution, so untrusted text lands in a string slot and cannot inject JSON structure; its path alphabet and header name are validated and a broken template is a queue-scope readiness refusal. Proven by tests/mythos-bridge-whatsapp-notify-test.js (131 checks) and tests/mythos-bridge-whatsapp-resilience-test.js (101 checks, incl. the WAHA generic mapping and the wa-evolution 201 reply); no real message sent by either.
records.othmode_usage: GitHub bridge terminal-state notifications only. Explicitly NOT MYTHOS AUTO WhatsApp / customer chat; every adapter implements sendText and nothing else.
records.verdict: BUILD the adapter boundary (about 400 lines, no dependency) + ADOPT Evolution API as the default runtime provider, PROVISIONALLY — decision re-affirmed on VERIFIED data by WA-PROVIDER-2 (2026-09-04): nothing is replaced because nothing is yet PROVEN on this host, no longer because nothing could be verified. Shortlist for gate step 3 (measure under a hard --memory cap for a week): (1) WAHA with the NOWEB or GOWS engine = the SAFE candidate (Apache-2.0, monthly releases, two maintainers), driven by providers/generic.js with PATH=/api/sendText, AUTH_HEADER=X-Api-Key, BODY={"session":"{{instance}}","chatId":"{{to}}@c.us","text":"{{text}}"}, ID_PATH=id — no code change; (2) wa-evolution = the LIGHT candidate (9.6 MB image, one process, SQLite), whose sendText contract is byte-identical to Evolution's so providers/evolution.js drives it unchanged — but it is a two-month-old, zero-star, single-author protocol re-implementation, so adopting it is an explicit owner risk decision. Evolution API itself: its stated 2 GB minimum plus Postgres + Redis is not met by this host today, and its licence addendum requires a visible usage notice if deployed. MultiWA and WaSphere exist (28 and 49 stars, MIT) but are larger multi-tenant gateways, not lighter ones: identified, not shortlisted. Search First evidence unchanged: no existing MYTHOS component sends WhatsApp; the nearest reusable pattern is the orchestrator ntfy notify() boundary (projects/mythos-orchestrator/runner.js).
records.before_deployment: Gate (docs/MYTHOS_WHATSAPP_PROVIDER_STRATEGY.md §6): step 1 resolve the swap exhaustion (re-read 2026-09-04: swap 4095/4095, 1,035 MiB available, Resource Guard CRITICAL) — NOT done; step 2 live-verify candidates — DONE 2026-09-04 (re-run if >60 days pass before step 3); step 3 measure the shortlisted candidate(s) under a hard --memory cap for a week with docker stats — NOT done; step 4 drive it through providers/generic.js (WAHA) or providers/evolution.js (wa-evolution) against a local recorder; step 5 keep the fences (loopback/RFC1918 host, 0600 credential, no unit file with configuration in Git; for wa-evolution set WA_APIKEY and never publish the unauthenticated /manager dashboard); step 6 the single controlled real message via mythos-github-bridge notify-test --confirm; step 7 no auto-merge, no automatic production deployment.

records.name: Customer inbox / CRM component for MYTHOS AUTO WhatsApp communication (Chatwoot selected; WaCRM rejected; Evolution / WAHA scoped as gateways behind the CRM)
records.source: github (self-hosted inbox/CRM) — live-verified via api.github.com and vendor documentation
records.repository: chatwoot/chatwoot · rejected: ArnasDon/wacrm · gateways (already in the WhatsApp notification record above): evolution-foundation/evolution-api, devlikeapro/waha
records.version: Chatwoot v4.17.1 (2026-08-27; pushed 2026-09-04) · WaCRM: no releases (pushed 2026-08-31) · Evolution 2.3.7 · WAHA 2026.8.2
records.license: Chatwoot: MIT core, enterprise/ directory under the Chatwoot Enterprise licence (GitHub NOASSERTION) · WaCRM: MIT · Evolution: Apache-2.0 + additional conditions (usage notice) · WAHA: Apache-2.0
records.purpose: Provide the customer-facing WhatsApp inbox, agents, assignment, contacts, labels, notes, history, templates, REST API and webhooks for MYTHOS AUTO projects (ssangyong.autos first; piece.autos, casse.autos), so that MYTHOS is the intelligence/orchestration layer and never the WhatsApp client.
records.integration_method: NOT vendored, NOT deployed. Built: projects/automotive/comms/ — provider-independent envelope (customer.message.received, privacy_class CUSTOMER_PII), multi-project configuration (one CRM, projects by Chatwoot account/inbox, *_file credentials only, private-host fence, unofficial provider acknowledgement), Chatwoot adapter (URL-token webhook authorisation in constant time, message_created parsing verified against message.rb#webhook_data, sendReply = POST /api/v1/accounts/{a}/conversations/{c}/messages with api_access_token), router with the business handler boundary (built-in handoff; throw/timeout/malformed → handoff; auto_reply per project default OFF; deliver sends only what the router allowed), CLI config-check / dry-run (never sends). Reuses bridge/notify/http-json.js, isPrivateHost and the shared redact; nothing under bridge/notify/ changed and the customer layer never uses the notification providers (asserted by tests/mythos-auto-comms-test.js, 113 checks).
records.status: SELECTED (designated), NOT DEPLOYED — BLOCKED on host resources
dependencies: a Chatwoot instance reachable on a private network (loopback / RFC1918 / WireGuard) — not deployed
a WhatsApp Business Platform (Cloud API / 360dialog) inbox in Chatwoot, or an Evolution/WAHA API-channel inbox with unofficial_acknowledged: true
records.maintenance: LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-09-05: Chatwoot 36,501 stars, 1,355 open issues, monthly releases, pushed 2026-09-04; Rails + Sidekiq + PostgreSQL + Redis, vendor minimum 4 GB RAM + 1 GB swap for a single-box install. WaCRM 2,231 stars, 33 open issues, single dominant maintainer, no releases, Next.js 16 + Supabase, Cloud API only, ships its own AI assistant. Evolution and WAHA both ship a native Chatwoot integration (API-channel inbox).
records.security: Chatwoot webhooks are unsigned: gated by a ≥16-char shared token in the URL (constant-time compare against a 0600 file) AND the private-host fence; egress refuses non-private hosts (unless allow_public), non-numeric ids, missing token, empty/oversized text; the API token exists only as a header for one postJson call and is in no result or log; customer text and names never in summaries; handler entities pass redact; handler error messages are reduced to a name. No governance-protected path, no credential-named file (token files are *.token via *_file keys).
records.othmode_usage: MYTHOS AUTO customer communication only. Explicitly NOT the GitHub bridge notification layer (separate record above, separate number, separate gateway). No second uncontrolled WhatsApp gateway: the CRM owns the only customer WhatsApp connection.
records.verdict: ADOPT Chatwoot as the inbox/CRM component and BUILD the thin MYTHOS boundary (envelope + adapter + router, about 700 lines, no dependency) — Search First: no existing MYTHOS component handles customer conversations; the nearest reusable pieces (http-json, isPrivateHost, redact) were reused, the notification adapter boundary (providers/generic.js) was deliberately NOT reused because it makes MYTHOS the WhatsApp client. REJECT WaCRM as CRM (fork-and-brand template, Supabase second auth/DB stack, no releases, competing AI layer). Provider preference: official Meta Cloud API through Chatwoot; unofficial only per explicit project acknowledgement; the router refuses an unofficial provider declared on a Channel::Whatsapp inbox. Deployment BLOCKED 2026-09-05 01:06 UTC: MemAvailable 2,729/7,746 MiB, swap 3,538/4,095 used (557 free), disk 88 % (9.4 GiB free) vs Chatwoot 4 GB + 1 GB swap — owner decides second VPS / managed Chatwoot behind the private fence, or RAM increase + swap resolution. Then: AUTO-COMMS-1 receiver service + runbook (docs/MYTHOS_AUTO_WHATSAPP_CRM_ARCHITECTURE.md §9).

records.name: Admin/data-management panel foundation for MYTHOS WP (Refine resource/dataProvider pattern + shadcn/Kiranism dashboard IA adopted as patterns; no framework vendored)
records.source: github — pattern review of refinedev/refine (resources + dataProvider + headless CRUD hooks), Kiranism/next-shadcn-dashboard-starter (rail/topbar/command-menu/data-table IA), shadcn/ui (component vocabulary); Payload CMS considered and rejected
records.version: pattern-level reuse only; no package installed (checked 2026-09-05)
records.license: refine: MIT · next-shadcn-dashboard-starter: MIT · shadcn/ui: MIT · Payload: MIT
records.purpose: Give MYTHOS WP (wp.mythosprod.xyz) a professional back-office shape — one declarative resource registry driving generic list / detail / create / edit / delete, server-side search, sort, filters, pagination, column visibility, command menu, record editor with shared validation — without introducing React/Next.js, Tailwind or a CMS into a repository whose services are dependency-light Node http + pg and whose design system is CSS-token based.
records.integration_method: NOT vendored, NO dependency added. projects/mythos-wp/reference/resources.js (registry) + crud.js (data provider) + web/js/table.js, form.js, command.js implement the same separation in plain JS on the canonical MYTHOS tokens. Only runtime dependency of the service: pg (already used by three sibling services).
records.decision: Next.js/React/Refine runtime REJECTED for this host and repository: no React anywhere in mythos-prod, design system is assets/brand/tokens.css + ERP component layer (CSS), and a Next build on a host with ~2.8 GiB available and an OOM history (mythos-memwatch) is an avoidable production risk. Payload CMS REJECTED: the catalogue already has a schema and a database; a CMS would be a second source of truth.

final_review: 2026-08-26 final Search First re-check: every manually built capability (evolution store, sessions, detectors, export) was re-searched against GitHub/PyPI/npm/MCP/Anthropic Skills; no maintained project matched the constraints (zero-dependency Node, fail-closed store semantics, no-exec runtime, GPL exclusion) better than the ~1.5k lines built — verdicts recorded per record above; no dependency added to inflate the registry. || 2026-09-04 SKILL-TRUST-0 Search First: skill/MCP security tooling re-searched (GitHub, PyPI, npm; NVIDIA first). Reused SkillSpector + SkillEvaluator Tier 1 + Gitleaks; deferred Semgrep (host memory) and SkillGuard; rejected the stale mcp-scan fork and snyk/agent-scan (data egress + external account). Built only adapters, a deterministic policy, content-bound ledgers and the executor gate (see docs/OTHMODE_SKILL_TRUST.md). || 2026-09-04 EXEC-ARCH-0 Search First: execution engines re-searched (OpenHands 1.16, mini-SWE-agent v2, SWE-agent, Goose) against the integrated Claude Code headless engine — all four REJECTED (API-key-only credential model, Docker/RAM footprint on a swap-full host, headless always-approve, and a parallel runtime that would bypass Skill Trust / MCP governance); Claude Code SELECTED as the single engine; Dagu SELECTED as the single scheduler for recurring host maintenance, superseding the bespoke autopilot reconciler of PR #158.
